title: Cycle 21: Keychain-persisted local auth + reactive 403 refresh
weak_spots: In-memory local auth token lost on app restart
BrowserOS token rotation caused 403 failures without auto-recovery
Concurrent reconnects could race to refresh the token
Keychain read failures could block chat entirely
competitors: OAuth2 single-flight refresh coordinator / Alamofire RequestRetrier
A2A security schemes: API key, Bearer, OAuth2 Client Credentials

variants.name: Keychain persistence + reactive 403 refresh
variants.summary: Store token in macOS Keychain; refresh once on 403 in SSE and A2A data paths; single-flight refresh deduplicates concurrent retries.

variants.name: Server-side stable device-paired token
variants.summary: BrowserOS mints a stable device-paired token; TriOS fetches once and only rotates on explicit server header. Needs server changes.

variants.name: Route-scoped capability tokens
variants.summary: Short-lived per-capability tokens (chat:stream, a2a:registry, etc.) for least privilege. Higher complexity.

lessons: Use a protocol-based token store so tests can swap in an in-memory store and failure scenarios are deterministic.
Actor-isolated single-flight refreshTask is the simplest Swift concurrency primitive for deduplicating forced token refreshes.
Always clean up stray .bak/.tmp source files before swift test or clade-audit; they break package discovery.
Catching domain-specific 403 transport errors in SSETransport and retrying once with forceRefresh=true closes the stale-token loop without server changes.
